question: The recent deaths of several white storks around the Manzanares river due to highly pathogenic avian influenza exposes serious shortcomings in health and environmental risk management in the Community of Madrid.

Despite the fact that this disease is covered by EU animal health legislation, there has been public criticism over the lack of clear protocols and information for emergency services, as well as the way that regional emergency authorities have downplayed the risk to citizens.

Regulation 2016/429 on animal health establishes obligations on surveillance, early detection, notification and coordination in relation to communicable diseases, including those that affect wild birds. In addition, Directive 2009/147/EC requires significant disruptions and mortality rates in protected species to be avoided. In light of the above: 1.
In the Commission’s view, does management by regional authorities comply with the diligence, surveillance and communication obligations set out in EU law?
Does the Commission consider the lack of clear protocols and information for emergency services to constitute a failure to comply with EU animal health legislation?
Does the Commission intend to take action when insufficient regional management of outbreaks in wildlife threatens public health and trust in EU warning systems?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) Infection with highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses in wild birds in Spain was detected based on surveillance performed by the competent authority of Spain.

Outbreaks were duly notified in the Animal Diseases Notification System in a timely manner and carcasses of dead wild birds in outbreaks were subject to disposal in accordance with the requirements of the EU animal health legislation1. The Commission has no grounds to suspect that the Spanish competent authorities did not comply with those rules.
1 Regulation (EU) 2016/429 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on transmissible
animal diseases and amending and repealing certain acts in the area of animal health (‘Animal Health Law’) (OJ L 84, 31.3.2016, pp. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/429/oj).
